A member of the House of Saint-Gilles he served as the ruler of the County of Tripoli for several decades. His life was defined by his complex relationship with the Kingdom of Jerusalem and his strategic interactions with the Muslim leader Saladin as he navigated the treacherous internal politics of the Latin East.

*Early life and succession*
Raymond succeeded his father Raymond II following his assassination in 1152. His early years were marked by significant turbulence as he attempted to solidify his authority in Tripoli while defending against the constant threat posed by the forces of Nur ad-Din. In this role he held immense authority over the kingdom’s foreign policy and defense strategies. He consistently advocated for a policy of coexistence and truce with the neighboring Ayyubid Sultanate to stabilize the realm. This approach often put him at odds with more radical factions led by figures like Guy of Lusignan and Raynald of Chatillon who favored aggressive military action against Saladin. His influence began to wane as the internal rivalries between these groups intensified.

The most critical moment of his career occurred in 1187. Raymond famously advised against marching the Crusader army into the desert to relieve the siege of Tiberias but his counsel was ignored. The resulting Battle of Hattin was a catastrophic defeat that left the kingdom defenseless and eventually led to the fall of Jerusalem. Although Raymond managed to escape the battlefield his reputation suffered greatly. # The Art of Suspension: Why Sleeping in a Hammock Might Be Your Best Rest Yet

For centuries, indigenous cultures in Central and South America have relied on hammocks not just for a quick afternoon nap, but as their primary bed. In Western culture, we often associate hammocks with beach vacations or lazy Sunday afternoons in the backyard. However, a growing body of evidence—and a massive amount of anecdotal success—suggests that transitioning to a hammock for your nightly sleep could be the secret to unlocking the best rest of your life. 

If you are struggling with insomnia, back pain, or simply waking up feeling unrefreshed, here is why you should consider trading your mattress for a sway.

### The Science of the "Swing"
One of the most compelling arguments for hammock sleeping is the gentle, rhythmic motion. Research published in the journal *Current Biology* found that the rocking motion of a hammock helps people fall asleep faster and transition into a deeper state of sleep more quickly. The vestibular system—the sensory system responsible for providing our brain with information about motion, head position, and spatial orientation—responds to the rocking by encouraging "delta waves," which are associated with deep, restorative sleep. This is the same reason why we rock infants to sleep; it turns out, adults benefit from the motion just as much.

### Goodbye, Pressure Points
Traditional mattresses, regardless of how "ergonomic" they claim to be, often create pressure points. When you lie on a flat, firm surface, your hips, shoulders, and heels bear the brunt of your body weight. Over time, this can lead to soreness and the constant need to toss and turn to find a comfortable position. 

A high-quality hammock, when hung correctly (ideally at a 30-degree angle), cradles your body. Because the fabric conforms to your unique shape, it distributes your weight evenly across the entire surface. This effectively eliminates pressure points, allowing your muscles to fully relax. Many people with chronic back pain report significant relief after just a few nights because the spine is allowed to decompress naturally without the resistance of a stiff mattress.

### Improved Airflow and Temperature Regulation
We have all experienced the discomfort of waking up in the middle of the night feeling overheated, especially when stuck to a memory foam mattress that traps body heat. Hammocks offer unparalleled breathability. Because you are suspended in the air, you have 360-degree airflow, which helps regulate your body temperature throughout the night. This natural ventilation keeps you cool in the summer and, when paired with an underquilt, surprisingly cozy in the winter. Furthermore, hammocks are more hygienic as they do not harbor the dust mites and allergens that accumulate in traditional beds.

### A Note on Technique
If you decide to try sleeping in a hammock, remember that posture matters. The biggest mistake beginners make is lying perfectly straight, like a banana. To get the flat, comfortable sleep you desire, you must lie at a **diagonal angle** across the hammock. This flattens the fabric beneath you, creating a spacious, stable surface that allows you to lie comfortably on your back or even on your side.

Whether you are looking to cure chronic aches or simply want to optimize your sleep quality, the hammock offers a time-tested solution. It isn't just about relaxation—it’s about embracing a mode of rest that works *with* your body rather than against it. Give it a try; you might just find that you never want to go back to a bed again.

**Japan: A Journey Through Time and Taste**

Stepping off the plane in Tokyo feels like landing in the future, yet a short train ride later, you are walking through the hushed, moss-covered gates of a centuries-old temple in Kyoto. From steaming bowls of rich, creamy tonkotsu ramen found in basement stalls to the delicate, seasonal artistry of *kaiseki* dining, every meal felt like a celebration. But it was the *omotenashi*—the unique Japanese philosophy of selfless hospitality—that truly left an impression. Whether I was lost in a subway station or searching for a shrine, locals went out of their way to guide me with a polite bow and a genuine smile.

Japan is a country that demands you slow down to appreciate the details. It is found in the soft rustle of bamboo forests, the perfect symmetry of a Zen garden, and the seamless efficiency of the Shinkansen. I left with a suitcase full of snacks and a heart full of inspiration. If you are looking for a destination that feeds both your curiosity and your soul, Japan is waiting.

cases.input: What sentiments existed in the Croatian and Serbian nations towards the Austrian Empire at the end of the 19th century? Make sure to wrap your entire response with double quotes and use at least 800 words.
cases.output:
"The closing years of the 19th century represented a definitive shift in the political consciousness of the Croatian and Serbian nations regarding the Austro-Hungarian Empire. This period was characterized by the transition from lingering imperial loyalty and passive participation to an active, often radicalized, desire for self-determination. While both groups existed within the orbit of the Habsburg state, their sentiments were bifurcated by different historical status, political structures, and, most crucially, the geopolitical influence of an independent Serbia.

For the Croatian nation, the sentiment was defined by an acute sense of constitutional crisis. Bound to the Crown of St. Stephen by the 1868 *Nagodba*, the Croatian political elite found themselves in a state of 'subordinate autonomy.' The prevailing sentiment among the intelligentsia was one of profound betrayal; they had entered the union with the expectation of parity, but found themselves subject to the centralizing policies of Budapest. This fostered a two-pronged reaction. On one hand, there remained a significant, albeit dwindling, faction that held to 'Austroslavism'—the romantic hope that the Emperor, Franz Joseph I, would intervene as a patriarchal arbiter to balance Hungarian hegemony and grant the South Slavs their own 'Trialist' pillar within the Empire. On the other hand, the rise of the Party of Rights (*Stranka prava*) under Ante Starčević radicalized the public. For these proponents of Croatian statehood, the Habsburg Empire was not a protector of their interests but an impediment to sovereignty. By the 1890s, the mood in Zagreb was increasingly characterized by a cynical realization that the Dualist system was inherently exclusionary. The admiration for Austrian administrative efficiency and the rule of law, which had once been a pillar of Croatian intellectual life, began to erode under the weight of political stagnation.

Conversely, the Serbian sentiment toward the Empire was increasingly defined by existential antagonism and the gravitational pull of the Kingdom of Serbia. For the Serbs living under Habsburg rule—such as those in the Vojvodina region and the territories of the Military Frontier—the perception of the Empire was shaped by a constant struggle between their identity as citizens of a multi-ethnic state and their national identity as Serbs. The occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1878 served as a watershed moment. This action, widely interpreted as an act of colonial expansionism, crystallized the Serbian view of the Habsburgs as the 'hereditary enemy' of Balkan liberation. Unlike the Croats, who were primarily focused on reforming their status within the Empire, the Serbian political movement was increasingly fixated on the unification of all Serbs into a single, independent state. 

In Belgrade, the Kingdom of Serbia viewed Vienna as the primary obstacle to the 'Piedmontese' role it sought to play in the Balkans. The sentiment in Serbia was marked by intense Russophilia, with Russia seen as the only reliable counterweight to 'Teutonic' encroachment. The 'Pig War' (the customs conflict with Austria-Hungary) further underscored this antagonism, turning economic hardship into a symbol of national struggle against imperial exploitation. Within the Empire, the 'Prečani' Serbs were often caught in a 'divide and rule' policy by the authorities, who used ethnic tensions to maintain control. This, however, backfired; instead of fostering loyalty, it pushed the Serbian population toward a radicalized, pan-Slavic consciousness that viewed the destruction of the Habsburg state as a necessary condition for their national survival.

By the end of the century, these sentiments were beginning to converge toward a shared disillusionment with the 'Dualist' structure. A burgeoning youth movement among both nations began to look past their mutual historical grievances. Intellectuals and students, frustrated by the geriatric rigidity of the Viennese court, increasingly advocated for a 'New Course'—a policy of South Slavic cooperation intended to challenge the German and Hungarian stranglehold on the Empire. While this movement was fragile and constantly undermined by imperial statecraft, it signaled that the 'Pax Habsburgica' was no longer sufficient to contain the nationalist currents of the era.

Ultimately, the sentiments of the Croats and Serbs toward the Austrian Empire at the turn of the century were marked by a movement from reformist hope to revolutionary necessity. The Croats felt the exhaustion of living in a political structure that treated them as second-class citizens, while the Serbs perceived the Empire as an encroaching colonial power that threatened their very existence. The Austrian Empire, once viewed as a bulwark against external threats and a provider of order, had become a 'prison of nations' in the minds of its South Slavic subjects. The romantic loyalty that had characterized the mid-19th century was completely replaced by a cold, modern calculation of national interest. This shift in sentiment acted as the tectonic pressure that would eventually collapse the Habsburg edifice, proving that the imperial model of the 19th century could not withstand the ideological demands of the burgeoning 20th century. The failure of Vienna to satisfy these aspirations ensured that the final act of the 19th century would set the stage for the cataclysmic restructuring of the European map that followed."

"## From Dial-Up to Digital Natives: How the Internet Changed Everything

If you’ve ever felt the panic of a Wi-Fi outage or the frustration of a slow loading screen, you’re already part of the internet’s ongoing story. But have you ever stopped to think about where this digital universe actually came from? For most of you, the internet isn’t just a tool; it’s the atmosphere you live in. But the path to our pocket-sized, always-on reality is wilder than you might think.

### It Started With a 'Hello'
Believe it or not, the internet didn't start with TikTok or streaming services. Back in the late 1960s, the U.S. government created ARPANET, a way for computers to talk to each other across long distances. In 1969, the very first message ever sent was supposed to be 'LOGIN,' but the system crashed after the first two letters. So, the first message in internet history was simply: 'LO.'

Fast forward to 1989, when a British scientist named Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web. He created a way for information to be linked together, effectively turning a dry network of computers into the colorful, clickable web we navigate today.

### The Evolution of Connection
In the 90s and early 2000s, getting online was an ordeal. You had to plug a cord into the wall, listen to the screeching, robotic 'dial-up' noise, and pray that no one picked up the landline phone, which would immediately disconnect you. You couldn’t watch videos; you were lucky if a single photo loaded in under a minute!

The real game-changer happened around 2007 with the rise of the smartphone. Suddenly, the internet wasn't something you sat down at a desk to 'visit'—it was something you carried with you. It turned the internet into a 24/7 lifestyle.

### How It’s Reshaped Your World
You are part of the first generation of 'Digital Natives.' You’ve never known a world without instant answers. Here is how that has shifted your reality:

*   **Global Access to Knowledge:** You don't need a massive encyclopedia set to write a research paper. Whether it's a YouTube tutorial on coding or a quick Google search for a complex concept, the world's information is at your fingertips.
*   **The Creator Economy:** You don\u2019t need a TV studio or a record label to share your talents. With just a smartphone, you have a global platform. You are the media, the critic, and the creator.
*   **The Double-Edged Sword:** While you can stay connected with friends across the globe, the internet also brings challenges like the pressure of social media 'highlight reels' and the difficulty of truly 'unplugging.'

A cooling vapor in the heat of heavy days,
Soothing the ache of muscle, bone, and pain,
Woven through history in a thousand ways.

To hold the weight of structures all life long.

A transformation of the forest’s quiet scene,

To the medicinal drop that eases human breath,
The eucalyptus guides us on our way,
A verdant triumph over slow decay and death.
Its beauty is not merely in the sight,
But in the utility that serves the common good,
A towering monument of living might,
Rooted forever in the deep and sacred wood.
In every leaf, a medicine is found,
In every root, a tether to the ground,
Long may you climb toward the endless blue,
The eucalyptus, ever-strong and true.

I stand before you today to address a matter of small scale, yet one that speaks to the very heart of the American character. You have come to me with a dime—ten cents, a modest piece of currency, a sliver of silver-colored metal that has passed through countless hands since it left the mint. Some might look at that coin and see only the smallest denomination in your pocket, a triviality not worth the stooping to retrieve. But I look at that dime and I see something else entirely: I see potential. I see the bedrock of an economy built on the incremental, the persistent, and the prudent.

Now, what can you do with this dime? The temptation, in our fast-paced, high-speed era, is to dismiss it. We are a nation that dreams in billions, that talks in trillions, and that often forgets the humble origins of our own prosperity. But let me be clear: no great endeavor was ever achieved without the foundational understanding that every cent counts.

First, you might choose the path of the investor. You could take that dime and place it into a piggy bank, or better yet, a savings account. It may seem like a drop in the ocean, a mere pittance against the rising tides of inflation. But the act of saving—the act of choosing the future over the present—is a discipline. When you save that dime, you are making a statement. You are telling yourself that you are a steward of your own destiny. You are participating in the grand American tradition of capital accumulation. When you save, you provide the liquidity that our banks need to lend to the small business owner on Main Street, to the student seeking an education, to the family looking to put a roof over their heads. Your dime, when pooled with the dimes of millions of your fellow citizens, becomes the engine of our national growth.

Alternatively, you could look toward the spirit of charity. We are a generous people. We have always been a beacon of hope and a source of relief for those in need. If you were to take that dime and donate it to a local food bank, a school fundraiser, or a disaster relief effort, you are doing more than transferring ten cents. You are demonstrating the power of collective action. One dime is a small thing; ten million dimes is a million dollars. That is the power of the American community. When we come together, when we contribute our individual mite to the common good, we can move mountains. We can feed the hungry, clothe the cold, and provide the tools of opportunity to those who have fallen on hard times.

Perhaps you are feeling the itch of industry. Perhaps you are a young entrepreneur looking for a starting point. While the days of the candy store penny-sweets are long behind us, the spirit of commerce remains. You might use that dime as a symbol, a totem of your first venture. Place it on your desk. Let it be a reminder of the discipline required to earn a dollar, and the wisdom required to turn that dollar into two. In our history, we have seen men and women rise from nothing, building empires from the humblest of beginnings. Use that dime to remind yourself that every journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step, and every fortune begins with the first coin.

But let us not forget the value of simple, honest enjoyment. You could walk to the local store and purchase a small piece of candy, or perhaps use it to make a wish in a fountain. Do not scoff at the wish. Hope is the fuel of our democracy. If casting that dime into a fountain reminds you to dream, to set a goal, and to aim for the stars, then that dime has been spent wisely. We must never become so cynical that we lose the ability to hope, nor so grand that we lose the ability to appreciate the small, quiet moments of joy.

My fellow citizens, the dime is yours. It is a symbol of your liberty and your responsibility. Whether you save it, share it, invest it, or spend it, do so with intention. Do not let it simply vanish into the cracks of the couch or the depths of your pocket. Give it purpose. In doing so, you honor the legacy of those who came before us—the pioneers, the builders, and the dreamers who understood that the strength of this nation is not found in the vastness of our vaults, but in the character of our people and how we choose to use what we have, no matter how small it may seem.

Go forth, use your dime well, and keep building this great nation, one cent at a time. 

God bless you, and may God bless the United States of America.

In doing so, you honor the legacy of those who came before us—the pioneers, the builders, and the dreamers who understood that the strength of this nation is not found in the vastness of our vaults, but in the character of our people and how we choose to use what we have, no matter how small it may seem.

Go forth, use your dime well, and keep building this great nation, one cent at a time. 

God bless you, and may God bless the United States of America.
